title: A stylesheet with no @version directive compiles with a warning and still applies
statement: Omitting the @version line from a Semantic CSS stylesheet produces the status 'Valid with warnings' and the message 'Version-one stylesheets should start with @version 1;', and the stylesheet is applied in full: a versionless sheet exports byte-identically to the same sheet under @version 1;, while a genuinely fatal @version 2; exports byte-identically to having no stylesheet at all. MISSING_VERSION_DIRECTIVE is simply not in the compiler's fatal set.

handVerified.note: Both halves confirmed, including 'the stylesheet still applies', proved by four PDF exports: versionless 238691 bytes equals @version 1; 238691 bytes, and @version 2; 238747 bytes equals no stylesheet 238747 bytes. Note the report itself records that this produced NO board red: the scenario passes only because it was re-authored onto @version 2;, which is a genuinely fatal code.

source.howDecided: Today's origin/main head, read with `gh api repos/AmruthPillai/Reactive-Resume/commits/main`, is 3221afda, the same commit the 2026-08-21 hand verification tested. Zero commits landed in between, so there was no diff to analyse; every culprit line was re-read in the working tree at that commit instead. permalinkTested and permalinkToday are the same URL by construction. Re-read today with the report's corrected numbers: compile.ts:45-49 pushes MISSING_VERSION_DIRECTIVE at severity 'warning'; diagnostics.ts:125-131 lists the five fatal codes (DUPLICATE_VERSION_DIRECTIVE, INVALID_VERSION, RESOURCE_LIMIT, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, VERSION_MISMATCH) and MISSING_VERSION_DIRECTIVE is not among them; resolve.ts:126-133 drops to EMPTY_PRESENTATION only on a fatal diagnostic. The doc sentences are unchanged at applying-custom-styles.mdx:46 and :305-307.

newItems.title: [Bug] Custom Styles not working
newItems.note: Open, Cloud. A stylesheet that correctly starts with @version 1; does not take effect until a browser refresh. Same editor, unrelated mechanism; checked precisely because it would have been a duplicate if it were about the directive.

newItems.title: Semantic CSS color has no effect on section heading text or icon
newItems.note: Open, Cloud, version 5.2.6. Also correctly uses @version 1;. Included only to record that the recent Semantic CSS issues were read and none concerns the version directive.

queries: non-search sweep: 800-item local issue list, and the bodies of #3291, #3293, #3295, #3348 read in full

reevaluation: The observation is exactly right and reproduces, but on re-reading the two doc sentences it is measured against, this is not drift and there is nothing here a maintainer can act on. applying-custom-styles.mdx:46 is an instruction ('Keep @version 1; at the start of every stylesheet'), not a promise that omitting it is fatal, and :305-307 describes what happens on a fatal version error without claiming that a missing directive is one. The product's behaviour agrees with both: it nudges you toward the directive with a warning whose text is nearly the doc's own sentence, and it reserves fatality for actual version errors. The report's own cross-reference records that this produced no board red, and the one scenario in the area passes only because it was re-authored onto @version 2;. Filing it would put a maintainer through a reproduction to arrive at 'working as designed', which is precisely the kind of report that spends credit for the rest of the batch. Confidence in the source reading is high; confidence that it is a defect is low, and that is the reason for the skip.
notes: Deployment: verified against SELF-HOSTED at 3221afda through the builder's own Custom Styles editor and its Download PDF, with four exports compared by byte length (the SHA-256s differ because a PDF carries a creation timestamp). Recorded as verified-but-not-filable rather than dropped, so the observation survives if the docs are ever tightened to say the directive is required, at which point the same evidence becomes a real drift report. If anyone does revive it, note the report's stale cite: the corpus gave compile.ts:44-48; the block is :45-49.
